workload.scope: one decoder layer (layer 0), not the full model

ttft_note: Not meaningful at single-layer scope; prefill latency is reported instead.
prefill_note: S=512, taken verbatim from the us_per_token column of doc/optimized_decoder/perf_prefill.csv and doc/functional_decoder/perf_prefill.csv. Both CSVs are regenerated by tests/test_perf.py without the watcher; a watcher run inflates them ~8x. Both files are rewritten by every run of the perf tests; re-measurement moves the third significant figure, so these are the values on disk. The 'before' leg is the functional layer as it stands in this tree -- stage 02 keeps its router rewrite in optimized_decoder.py rather than in the shared functional_decoder.router_forward precisely so that this baseline does not drift with stage-02 work.
decode_device_note: 0.5127 ms is the sum of DEVICE KERNEL DURATION over rows 45-103 of ops_perf_optimized_decode.csv -- the last 59 rows, which are exactly the decode region (the capture is a 32-token prefill then one decode step); 0.5634 ms is the blocking traced replay in perf_decode.csv at ctx128. The 51 us difference is host dispatch inside the blocking replay. Op-count history of this region: 60 ops / 534.8 us before the section-7 router rewrite, which removed four ops and added two for 58 ops / 511.7 us, then the section-7 divisor guard added one for the 59 ops / 512.7 us on disk.
roofline_fraction_basis: 0.0822 / 0.5127 = 16.0% against device time; against the 0.5634 ms e2e replay it is 14.6%

roofline_inputs.active_expert_weights_detail: top-8 of 128 experts at bfloat4_b (0.5625 B/elem): gate_up 8*2048*1536 = 25165824 elem = 14.16 MB, down 8*768*2048 = 12582912 elem = 7.08 MB
roofline_inputs.attention_weights_detail: wqkv 2048*5120 = 10485760 elem = 11.14 MB + wo 4096*2048 = 8388608 elem = 8.91 MB at bfloat8_b (1.0625 B/elem). At the stage-01 bf16 dtype this term was 37.75 MB (20.97 + 16.78); an earlier revision of this file recorded 29.36, which was wrong at any dtype, and a later one recorded 18.88, which dropped the block exponents.
roofline_inputs.bandwidth_basis: back-derived from the measured rows: tt_perf_report_optimized_decode.txt row 49 (qkv) reports 384 GB/s at 74.9% of peak, i.e. 512 GB/s
roofline_inputs.note: expert weights bfloat4_b, attention projections bfloat8_b, norms/router/KV bf16
roofline_inputs.block_float_note: Block-float formats are counted at their true footprint, not at a round byte per element: a 32x32 tile is 576 B at bfloat4_b and 1088 B at bfloat8_b, i.e. 0.5625 and 1.0625 B/element, because each 16-element block carries its own exponent byte. An earlier revision of this file used 0.5 and 1.0 and reported total_mb 38.53 / estimate 0.0753 / fraction 0.141.
roofline_inputs.component_bytes_note: Exact, not rounded, and they sum to total_bytes with no residue. The _mb fields above are these divided by 1e6 and rounded to three places, so adding the _mb fields back up recovers total_mb only to that rounding -- component_bytes is the authority. Tile counts: gate_up 24576 and down 12288 tiles at 576 B (bfloat4_b), wqkv 10240 and wo 8192 tiles at 1088 B (bfloat8_b), router 2048*128 at 2 B (bf16). KV read is 2 (K and V) * 128 ctx * 4 kv-heads * 128 head_dim * 2 B = 262144.

named_limitations: sparse_matmul pads M to a full 32-row tile, so decode at M=1 performs 32x the necessary row work, and the three ReshapeView ops that compact the padding away are 111.12 us = 21.7% of decode device time. (The ReshapeViewDeviceOperation op-code line reads 22.3%; the extra 0.6 points is a fourth, 3.39 us reshape in the layer tail that is not part of the compaction.) output_tile=Tile([1,32]) removes the padding and is 1.07x faster, but no downstream op consumes a 1x32 tile correctly (slice rejects it, sum/reshape raise, untilize returns wrong data, fast_reduce_nc returns zeros). Blocked on TTNN, not on this model.
Prefill computes all 128 experts per 32-token chunk, forced by sparse_matmul indexing sparsity by batch dims rather than by M; the per-token alternative measured 2.1x slower.

Prefill attention uses an interleaved weight copy: MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCastDRAMShardedProgramConfig is decode-shaped (per_core_M=1), and a plain ttnn.linear cannot read a DRAM-sharded weight at all. Attention is 0.8% of prefill so this is not worth chasing.

Batch coverage runs to 32 in process (B = 1, 2, 8, 32, each user against its own HF reference). B=64 is refused by ttnn: nlp_create_qkv_heads_decode_device_operation.cpp:51 asserts num_users <= num_users_supported with num_users_supported = 32 hardcoded at line 45, on the interleaved attention path as well as the DRAM-sharded one. The two earlier caps -- the test uploading the unused bf16 functional weight set, and decode's expert intermediates pinned to L1 -- were self-inflicted and are removed.

The router block (rows 69-88 of ops_perf_optimized_decode.csv) is still 88.9 us = 17.3% of decode after the section-7 rewrite and its divisor guard, and 50.8 us of that -- 57.2% of the block -- is TopK on one core (26.4 us; a single 128-wide row, nothing to spread) plus the router matmul on four (24.4 us; N=128 is 4 tiles, so it cannot use more). The one measured, adoptable item left is 3.1 us of tile<->row-major conversion around the scatter, which is blocked by sparse_matmul requiring ROW_MAJOR sparsity (sparse_matmul_device_operation.cpp:105) while every consumer of the same tensor as a scale requires TILE.
evidence: full suite: 79 passed (71 with the perf tests deselected)

adopted_policy.attention_decode_matmul: MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCastDRAMShardedProgramConfig, weight width-sharded one shard per DRAM bank (8 banks), L1 width-sharded activation and output. 8 is the tuned quantity; the profiler's CORE COUNT column reads 80 for these rows and tt-perf-report prints 12, and neither of those was chosen -- see the core-count table in README.md.
adopted_policy.visible_in_measured_rows: tt-perf-report rows 49 and 67 of tt_perf_report_optimized_decode.txt -- which are rows 47 and 65 of ops_perf_optimized_decode.csv, the report's ID column running two ahead of the CSV line number: 'LoFi BF16 x BFP8 => BF16' at 384 and 383 GB/s (74.9% and 74.8% of peak), 27.33 and 21.91 us. The like-for-like interleaved rows are 50 and 67 of functional_decoder/tt_perf_report_decode_paged32.txt -- 57.06 us at 73.4% for qkv and 72.80 us at 46.1% for wo. Only wo was SLOW-classified; qkv was already DRAM-classified interleaved, so the win there is the 2.08x drop in duration, not a change of class. The experts are report rows 92 and 100 (CSV rows 90 and 98): 'LoFi BF16 x BFP4 => BF16' on 48 and 64 cores. An earlier revision of this file cited 'rows 50 and 68' and 'rows 94 and 102', which were report IDs from the previous profile quoted as CSV rows.
adopted_policy.router: Top-k on raw fp32 logits, softmax over the 8 survivors only, and neither reduction spelled as a ttnn reduction: the max is column 0 of the sorted top-k, and the sum is a matmul against a column of ones taken after the scatter, where the reduction length is num_experts=128 and therefore tile-aligned. ttnn.max/ttnn.sum each pull a 10.4 us FillPad behind 1.4 us of reduction on an 8-wide tensor. Worth 0.5866 -> 0.5615 ms on the traced layer at identical routing, before the +1.6 us divisor guard that section 7 also adopted; see work_log.md section 7.
